description: Hello, we're Tree Plex, compsci students from Indonesia. We joined the Field Shift challenge because farming in Indonesia is getting harder as rain seasons keep shifting and many families farm less than half a hectare. We built TANI, an app that uses NASA data to help small farmers compare crop rotations for their own field, so they can protect their soil, save water and choose what to plant and when.
summary:
TANI is a crop rotation decision support tool for small farms in Indonesia. A farmer outlines a field on satellite imagery and enters the usual planting order, start month, planning period and water source. TANI reads ten years of NASA POWER daily climate data (2016 to 2025) and SoilGrids soil data for that field, then checks the usual rotation and ten candidate rotations against temperature, soil pH, planting order and rainfall rules. It shows the usual rotation next to up to three alternatives chosen for saving water, caring for soil or estimated revenue. Each option comes with a month by month calendar, how often rain was enough in past years, bare months, risks and an estimated sales value from 2023 national prices. Cropy, an AI assistant, answers follow-up questions about saved fields.

TANI addresses Field Shift by turning NASA Earth observations, local soil data, crop characteristics and farmer priorities into rotation choices that are easy to compare. It matters because more than half of Indonesia's 28.4 million farm households work less than half a hectare and face shifting rain seasons. TANI supports, and does not replace, farmers and local extension officers.
details:
What it does and how it works

TANI helps small farmers in Indonesia compare crop rotations for their own field.

  • Mark the field. Search a village or type coordinates, then tap the corners of the field on satellite imagery.
  • Fill in the plan. Enter the usual planting order, the start month, a planning period of 6 to 24 months and whether the field is rainfed or irrigated.
  • Read NASA and soil data. The backend reads ten complete years (2016 to 2025) of NASA POWER daily rain, temperature, humidity and solar radiation, plus SoilGrids 2.0 soil pH, organic carbon and texture in the top 30 cm.
  • Check the rules. The usual rotation and ten candidate rotations are checked for a valid calendar, crop temperature limits, soil pH, planting order, and whether rain reached each crop's water need in at least 60% of the reference years.
  • Pick alternatives. Up to three options are selected: one for saving water, one for caring for the soil and one for the highest estimated revenue.
  • Compare and explain. The results page shows the field through the season month by month, the soil, five dimensions side by side (climate fit, water pressure, bare months, soil contribution and risks), the reasons behind every strategy and an estimated sales value from 2023 national prices and yields.
  • Ask Cropy. An AI assistant answers follow-up questions and can open a signed in user's saved fields.

Benefits and intended impact

Most Indonesian farm households work less than half a hectare, and many fields depend on rain. TANI turns long term NASA data into choices a farmer can discuss with a local extension officer:

  • When a second crop is likely to run short of water
  • Which rotation leaves the field bare for fewer months
  • Which option adds a legume for the soil
  • What each option may earn

We want farmers to adapt planting to shifting rain seasons with evidence from their own field, not only from habit.

Tools and technology

  • Frontend: Next.js 16, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, MapLibre GL, Terra Draw and Turf for drawing and measuring fields, Framer Motion for animation
  • Backend: Python, FastAPI, Pydantic, rasterio and httpx
  • Data: NASA POWER, ISRIC SoilGrids 2.0, FAO ECOCROP crop limits, Ministry of Agriculture of Indonesia price and yield statistics, Esri World Imagery and Nominatim
  • Storage and deployment: PostgreSQL for accounts and saved fields, Docker on a VPS for the backend, Vercel for the frontend, GitHub Actions to test and deploy every change
  • Testing: Playwright and pytest cover the main flows
  • Hardware: no special hardware was used

What makes it creative

  • Field level, not region level. Most planting calendars give advice for a whole region. TANI works on the plot the farmer draws.
  • Starts from what the farmer already does. The usual rotation is always shown next to the alternatives.
  • Easy to follow. The season plays as an animated field, month by month.
  • Clear evidence. Every result states how often rain was enough, for example 8 of 9 years, instead of a single score.

Factors we considered

  • Small plots and rainfed fields
  • Honest uncertainty: results are historical frequencies, not forecasts
  • No combined score that hides trade offs
  • Indonesian and English text
  • Simple steps for users with little map experience
  • Cached data so the demo works without slow external services
  • A clear reminder that local farmers and extension officers make the final decision

Use of SI

Our team defined the problem, the method and the user experience. SI tools supported parts of the coding and documentation. Inside the app, a language model writes the strategy explanations and powers Cropy. The rule engine and all NASA and soil values are not generated. SI-generated images are labelled where they appear.
